guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Give a new interest enough repetitions to get past the humiliation of being a beginner. You may quit because you genuinely dislike it. You may also discover a part of yourself that never had permission to exist. This is pl/ork in its most literal form: play becomes part of identity formation.
brief:
- give a new interest enough repetitions to get past the humiliation of being a beginner ("enough", no number; not an endurance test)
- you may quit because you genuinely dislike it (real dislike, not the humiliation or the critic talking)
- you may also discover a part of yourself that never had permission to exist ("may", "a part", not the one true self)
- this is pl/ork in its most literal form: play becomes part of identity formation ("part of"; the article defines pl/ork already)
- context, not for the text: two first drafts of this paragraph failed. In one, every sentence moved the steps along with nothing to break them (no reaction, pause, allowance, or stopping to wonder what something would feel like). The other packed its question into a list of three and stacked coach phrases.
